![Illustration from [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-institute-agenda).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

Anthropic [published](https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-institute-agenda) the research agenda for The Anthropic Institute (TAI) on May 7, 2026. The premise: a frontier lab can see AI's real-world effects earlier than outside researchers can, and TAI's job is to publish those signals so external organizations, governments, and the public can act on them. Outputs are described as inputs to the [Long-Term Benefit Trust](https://www.anthropic.com/news/the-long-term-benefit-trust) (LTBT) and to release decisions, with the Anthropic Fellowship as the recruitment surface. The LTBT is an independent five-trustee body that, via a special Class T share, elects a growing share of Anthropic's board (a majority within four years); its remit was announced as long-range and extreme-event decisions, not day-to-day operations.

The agenda lays out four pillars:

- **Economic diffusion.** Higher-cadence and more granular data from the [Anthropic Economic Index](https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index) as an "early warning signal for significant change and disruption". Open questions:
  - adoption inequality across countries;
  - firm-level concentration of AI usage;
  - productivity growth;
  - how junior-role pipelines train senior practitioners once AI absorbs the entry-level tasks.
- **Threats and resilience.** Topics feeding the [Frontier Red Team](https://red.anthropic.com/) and [Project Glasswing](https://www.anthropic.com/glasswing) backlog, framed by an explicit asymmetric tempo (capabilities advance in months, regulatory and insurance responses on years):
  - dual-use observability;
  - market-based risk pricing;
  - offense-defense balance in cyber and bio;
  - crisis-coordination infrastructure for AI scenarios.
- **AI systems in the wild.**
  - group epistemology when most users consult the same few models;
  - critical-thinking degradation under increasing deference;
  - governance of autonomous agents, with naval-law analogies for unattended ships;
  - AI oversight of AI.
- **AI-driven R&D.**
  - telemetry for measuring research speedup;
  - "fire drill" tabletop exercises for an intelligence-explosion scenario;
  - who governs systems that build their successors;
  - a separate "jagged frontier" question on whether models can be steered toward high-externality science (drug discovery, materials) that markets underweight.

## My Notes

- **TAI is the field's first research-agenda layer.** Across the four frontier labs, [OpenAI's *Our principles*](/posts/20260428-openai-agi-principles/) and its peer documents map two existing document types: declared values and deployment gates. TAI is a third type, set up to produce empirical findings the other two layers can be checked against. The [Anthropic Economic Index](/posts/20260423-anthropic-economic-index/), with more granular data and higher cadence under TAI, is one concrete commitment. OpenAI's new "Adaptability" principle commits to updating positions as evidence accumulates; TAI is the closest the field has to an institution set up to produce that evidence.

- **Two ways TAI matters, both untested.**
  - **Externally,** the agenda promises an "early warning signal for significant change and disruption", language that asserts a verifiable measurement. If outsiders can't reproduce TAI's numbers from the published procedure, anyone acting on the early-warning claim has to take Anthropic's word for it.
  - **Internally,** TAI's findings feed into the LTBT, giving the Trust a steady research-policy stream beyond the extreme-event scope it was originally announced for. That integration becomes meaningful only when a Trust position publicly diverges from a commercial decision.

- **The R&D pillar's telemetry could check Clark's forecast.** [Jack Clark](/posts/20260508-import-ai-455-automating-ai-research/) put 60% on full AI-driven R&D by end of 2028 from public benchmark trends. TAI commits to publishing the internal R&D speedup data that would let outside readers compare that forecast to actual progress. Without publication, the pillar stays purely internal and only useful to Anthropic.
